title: Source module imports five Sui-framework members that are now provided by the default prelude — five W02021 'duplicate alias' warnings carry forward into every build
description: Sui 1.45+ provides implicit prelude aliases for `std::option::Option`, `sui::object::{Self, ID, UID}`, `sui::transfer`, and `sui::tx_context::TxContext`. The source module re-imports all five at the top of the file (lines 10, 15, 16, 17). The compiler emits five W02021 'duplicate alias' warnings on every `sui move build` — see green.log lines 66-112 for the exact emissions. The doc-first agent's 'Upgrade Outdated Code' rule explicitly calls out 'Explicit framework dependencies in Move.toml (Sui 1.45+ uses implicit)' as a Move 2024 modernisation target, and the same principle applies to prelude imports. The green-phase synthesis-notes.md already acknowledges this as 'unused-alias for sui::transfer and sui::tx_context::TxContext aliases that are now default in Sui 1.69 — quality nit' but the implementation has not been cleaned up. Removing the five redundant import members would cut the source from 9 imports to 4 (only `deepbook::pool::{Self, Pool}`, `sui::balance::{Self, Balance}`, `sui::clock::Clock`, `sui::coin::{Self, Coin}`, `sui::event`, `token::deep::DEEP` remain) and silence five lint emissions per build.
impact: Persistent build-time warning noise (five emissions per build). Consumers running `move-code-quality` will see the lint count and may treat it as a contract-vs-implementation discrepancy. Future maintainers will copy the redundant imports forward into new modules. AC3.6's 'Move 2024 quality pass reports no issues' verification is technically softened — the warnings are not errors but they are findings in the strict reading.

title: Source uses module-qualified function-call form (`pool::swap_exact_base_for_quote(pool, ...)`, `coin::value(&c)`, `balance::withdraw_all(&mut b)`) instead of Move 2024 dot-method-call idiom — same finding as Cycle 2 R2-003 carried forward
description: Eleven call-sites in this module use the legacy module-qualified function-call form when their first parameter is the receiver, for which Move 2024 supports dot-method-call syntax. Concrete sites: line 76 `coin::value(&coin)` → `coin.value()`; line 80 `object::new(ctx)` (no receiver — keep as-is); line 82 `coin::into_balance(coin)` → `coin.into_balance()`; line 90 `object::id(&vault)` → `vault.id()` (works because `Vault<T>` has `key`, framework derives `id` accessor) — but Sui's `object::id` is the canonical helper; both forms are accepted; line 113 `balance::withdraw_all(&mut vault.balance)` → `vault.balance.withdraw_all()`; line 114 `coin::from_balance(balance, ctx)` → `balance.from_balance(ctx)` is NOT idiomatic (the receiver is the wrapping target not `Balance`); line 140 `object::id(vault)` → `vault.id()` per above; line 144 same as 113; line 145 same as 114; lines 152-154 `coin::value(&...)` → `<coin>.value()`; line 150 `pool::swap_exact_base_for_quote(pool, ...)` → `pool.swap_exact_base_for_quote(...)` (DeepBook's signature is `self: &mut Pool`, dot-syntax is supported and the upstream code itself uses it); line 179 `balance::value(&vault.balance)` → `vault.balance.value()`. The doc-first agent rules call this out as a Move 2024 upgrade target ('Old function-style calls (`vector::push_back(&mut v, x)` → `v.push_back(x)`)'). Cycle 2 R2-003 raised the identical pattern against `slippage_swap.move` and the cycle 3 implementation has not picked up the carry-forward fix. Migrating these sites also lets the imports block drop the `Self` member from `use sui::balance::{Self, Balance}` → `use sui::balance::Balance`, `use sui::coin::{Self, Coin}` → `use sui::coin::Coin`, and `use deepbook::pool::{Self, Pool}` → `use deepbook::pool::Pool` (the only `Self::` use is `pool::swap_exact_base_for_quote` on line 150).
impact: Style drift from Move 2024 idioms; carries forward three unnecessary `Self` imports; each pattern repetition makes future maintainers copy the legacy form into new modules. Cycle 2 R2-003 was raised but not formally accepted/rejected — Cycle 3 inherits the same finding. Not a correctness issue.
recommendation: Refactor in one pass: (a) drop `Self` from the three imports; (b) migrate the eleven call-sites to dot-syntax per the mapping above (skip `coin::from_balance` and `object::new` which are constructors not receivers). Re-run `sui move test -e localnet` to confirm 7/7 PASS preserved. Single-commit refactor; mechanically guaranteed safe because dot-syntax is sugar for the qualified form when the receiver type matches.

title: Public read-accessor surface is asymmetric — `TriggerFired.base_residual_amount` and `TriggerFired.deep_residual_amount` lack accessors while every other event field has one
description: The module exposes 11 read-accessor functions for the two events: 7 for `VaultCreated` (vault_id, owner, pool_id, side, tp_price, sl_price, deposit_amount — covers all 7 fields) and 4 for `TriggerFired` (vault_id, owner, current_price, quote_out_amount — covers 4 of 6 fields). The two missing `TriggerFired` accessors are `trigger_fired_base_residual_amount` and `trigger_fired_deep_residual_amount`. This asymmetry is a design defect: either the accessor surface is the public-API contract for downstream consumers (Cycle 3b keeper, Cycle 3c UI, off-chain indexers — all of which read events out-of-band) and should be complete, or it is purely a test convenience and should be `#[test_only]` (which would let the implementer drop the public surface entirely and still let tests inspect fields via the `Self` import). The current state — public, partial — is the worst of both worlds: downstream consumers cannot read residual amounts via the canonical accessor pattern, and the public surface advertises an obligation that is not honoured uniformly. Note: the test suite currently does not assert on residual amounts (T-004/T-005 `take_from_sender<Coin<SUI>>` and `take_from_sender<Coin<DEEP>>` without value assertions, lines 268-272 and 365-369), so the missing accessors are not test-blocking — but if E-007's Cycle 3b stub→real promotion or the keeper-side reconciliation logic in Cycle 3b needs to read `base_residual_amount` from a `TriggerFired` for skim-detection logic, the accessor will be needed.
impact: Inconsistent public surface advertises an incomplete event-read API. Downstream consumers (keeper / UI / indexer) reading `TriggerFired` via the accessor pattern have to fall back to module-internal field access (which `copy, drop, store` already permits but is non-idiomatic) or call BCS-decode on the raw event bytes. Future maintainers will not know whether the omission was intentional. Asymmetric surface fails the Move-Book code-quality checklist's 'public surface — only what's needed, all of what's documented' test.
recommendation: Either: (a) add the two missing accessors `pub fun trigger_fired_base_residual_amount(evt: &TriggerFired): u64 { evt.base_residual_amount }` and the matching `_deep_residual_amount` to make the surface symmetric (preferred — it costs ~6 LOC and makes the API uniform); or (b) move ALL 11 accessors behind `#[test_only]` since downstream consumers in Cycles 3b/3c read events off-chain via SuiClient (where Move accessors are irrelevant) — this would correctly express that the accessors exist for in-tree test convenience only. Pick (a) if the keeper / UI need a uniform on-chain read API; pick (b) if event consumption is exclusively off-chain. The code as written commits to neither.

title: 11 public read-accessors for event fields plus 2 vault accessors are exposed unconditionally — should be `#[test_only]` since downstream consumers read events off-chain
description: Lines 175-234 declare 13 public functions (`balance_value`, `is_triggered`, plus 11 event accessors) whose only consumers in this cycle are the in-tree `tests/tpsl_vault_tests.move` file. The events `VaultCreated` and `TriggerFired` have abilities `copy, drop, store` (lines 45 and 55), which means any code in the package — including `#[test_only]` modules — can read fields directly via the `evt.field_name` form without needing public accessors. The public-accessor pattern is necessary only when (a) consumers are external Move modules outside the package (none in this slot) or (b) the event needs to abstract internal representation. Neither applies here. Exposing them unconditionally inflates the package's public API surface from 3 entries (`create_vault`, `withdraw`, `execute_trigger`) to 16 entries, of which 13 are pure-projection getters that cannot be removed in a future upgrade without breaking compatibility. The Move Book's `book/guides/upgradeability-practices.md` warns against exposing more public surface than is contractually obligated. Note this is largely cosmetic given Cycle 3b/3c consume events via SuiClient.queryEvents (off-chain RPC, no Move accessor involved) — but the public API obligation is real once the package is published.
impact: Inflates the package's permanent public API by 13 entries. Future package upgrades must preserve all 13 signatures or risk breaking external consumers (none today, but the accessors are public). Future maintainers will not know which accessors are 'load-bearing for the keeper' vs 'test-only conveniences'. Cycle 3b's keeper consumes `TriggerFired` via SuiClient subscribeEvent / queryEvents (off-chain JSON), where the public Move accessor is irrelevant.
recommendation: Move the 11 event accessors and the 2 vault accessors into a `#[test_only]` block at the bottom of the module, OR put them in a sibling `#[test_only] module tpsl_vault::tpsl_vault_test_helpers;` so test code stays clean while production surface stays minimal. The test module already imports the events (`use tpsl_vault::tpsl_vault::{Self, Vault, VaultCreated, TriggerFired};` line 19) so direct field access via the `Self` package qualifier (`evt.vault_id` works inside any module of the package) is available without changing tests at all — a simpler refactor would be to delete all 13 accessors and rewrite the 17 test call-sites to use direct field access. Either is correct; deleting is the smallest diff if the keeper / UI consume events strictly off-chain.

title: Three `public entry fun` declarations carry `#[allow(lint(public_entry))]` — contract-driven and correctly suppressed; documentation pointer back to the contract decision is missing in-tree
description: Per contract.md 'Contract decisions' #1 and AC3.6 NOTE 2, the spec mandates the literal word 'entry function', so `public entry fun` is used for `create_vault`, `withdraw`, and `execute_trigger`. The W99010 lint is suppressed correctly via `#[allow(lint(public_entry))]` on each function (lines 67, 108, 124). This is the same finding as Cycle 2 R2-001, correctly carried forward and applied. However, the in-tree `#[allow]` attributes carry no comment explaining why the suppression is required. Cycle 2 R2-001's recommendation was: 'Add `#[allow(lint(public_entry))]` immediately above the `public entry fun` declaration, with a one-line comment: `// AC3.2/3.3/3.4 mandate `public entry`; suppress W99010 for spec-compliance.`' The current implementation has the suppression but not the documenting comment. A future maintainer running `move-code-quality` and seeing the `#[allow]` will not know it traces back to AC3.2/3.3/3.4 + Contract decisions #1 — they may delete the suppression assuming it was a temporary measure.
impact: Without the documenting comment, the suppression is a bare `#[allow]` that future maintainers may strip on the assumption it was a temporary lint-shut-up. If they then 'fix' the lint by removing `entry`, AC3.2/3.3/3.4's verbatim 'entry function' verification breaks. The in-tree comment is the only durable mechanism that keeps the contract decision discoverable to readers without the cycle artifacts handy.
recommendation: Add a one-line comment immediately above each `#[allow(lint(public_entry))]`, citing the specific AC. E.g., for line 67: `// AC3.2 mandates the verbatim word 'entry function'; W99010 suppressed per Contract decision #1.` Repeat for lines 108 (cite AC3.3) and 124 (cite AC3.4). This makes the spec-compliance rationale durable in-tree.

title: Move.toml drops `deepbook_margin` with an inline comment — same Cycle-2 deviation correctly carried forward; comment could cite the friction-log entry by line for traceability
description: The Move.toml correctly carries forward Cycle 2's `deepbook_margin` exclusion with an inline 4-line comment (lines 9-13) explaining the bundled `deepbook_margin/tests/helper/test_helpers.move` references the missing `pyth::price_info::new_price_info_object_for_test` symbol. This matches contract.md's 'In scope' Move.toml expectations and the Cycle 2 R2-002 carry-forward. The comment is well-written and self-documenting. Minor improvement: per Cycle 2 R2-002 recommendation, the comment could cite the friction-log entry by line and date (e.g., `# carry-forward of Cycle 2 R2-002; see independent/raw-friction.log [deepbook] entry`) so a future maintainer running `git blame` on the Move.toml can trace the deviation back to the originating cycle artifact without having to grep the .forge/ directory. Not a defect — informational confirmation that the design choice is correct.
impact: None for correctness. The omission is fully documented inline. Minor traceability gap if a future cycle re-evaluates whether `deepbook_margin` can be re-added (which would require checking whether the upstream pyth helper has been added — that check is easier when the comment cites the friction-log line).
recommendation: Optional: append `# (carry-forward of Cycle 2 R2-002 / R3-001; check independent/raw-friction.log [deepbook] before re-adding)` to the comment block. Single-line change; no functional impact.

title: Vault<phantom T> uses phantom correctly for the Balance<T> wrapping pattern; struct field ordering and ability set match Move 2024 conventions
description: Confirmation note: the `Vault<phantom T>` declaration (line 32) correctly applies the `phantom` keyword. `T` parameterises only the wrapped `Balance<T>` field — it never appears in another field nor is it stored as a value type — so `phantom` is the correct ability-marker (per Move Book `book/move-basics/generics.md` 'Phantom Type Parameters': 'When a type parameter does not appear inside a non-phantom-marked struct field, it should be marked phantom'). Without `phantom`, a `Vault<NonStoreType>` would be unconstructible because `T` would propagate ability requirements through every field. The ability set `has key` (no `store`) is correct: the vault is meant to live as a shared object only (line 102 `transfer::share_object(vault)`) and never to be wrapped as an inner field of another struct. Field order — `id`, `owner`, `balance`, `tp_price`, `sl_price`, `pool_id`, `side`, `triggered` — matches contract.md AC3.1's enumerated field list and follows the conventional 'identity → ownership → custody → policy → metadata → lifecycle' top-down ordering. No design defect.
impact: None — confirms correct application of Move 2024 generics + ability conventions.
evidence:
/// Shared object that custodies a Balance<T> under owner-defined TP/SL prices.
public struct Vault<phantom T> has key {
    id: UID,
    owner: address,
    balance: Balance<T>,
    tp_price: Option<u64>,
    sl_price: Option<u64>,
    pool_id: ID,
    side: u8,
    triggered: bool,
}

title: `triggered: bool` lifecycle representation is acceptable for the one-way state machine — an `enum Lifecycle { Active, Triggered }` would be more expressive but is not required
description: Confirmation note with optional alternative: `triggered: bool` (line 40) represents the vault's binary lifecycle (Active → Triggered, one-way). This is correct, minimal, and matches contract.md AC3.1's 'triggered lifecycle flag' wording verbatim. An alternative Move 2024 idiom would be a `public enum Lifecycle has copy, drop, store { Active, Triggered }` field which (a) makes the state-machine self-documenting via the type name, (b) lets future cycles add states like `Cancelled` or `Expired` without breaking on-chain compatibility (enums in Move 2024 support additive variant extension on package upgrade per `book/move-basics/enum-and-match.md`), and (c) lets `execute_trigger` and `withdraw` use exhaustive `match` instead of negation-on-bool guards. The bool form is fine for this slot — it's one bit, fits the spec verbatim, and the state machine is provably one-way. The enum form is a 'nice to have' that becomes valuable if Cycle 4+ ever needs a third lifecycle state. No action required for AC3.1 compliance.
impact: None for AC3.1 compliance. Future-proofing only — if a third state is added later (e.g., 'cancelled by owner before trigger'), the bool form requires schema migration; the enum form is additive.
recommendation: No action for this cycle. If Cycle 4 or beyond adds a third lifecycle state, refactor at that point — Move 2024 enums are upgrade-safe additive. For Cycle 3 the bool is the right minimal expression.

title: Public surface contains only the three contract-mandated entry functions plus the two events plus 13 read-accessors — entry-function surface is correctly minimal; accessor surface inflation tracked in R2-003 / R2-004
description: Confirmation note for the entry-function surface: the module declares exactly three public entry functions (`create_vault`, `withdraw`, `execute_trigger`) — matching contract.md's 'In scope' section verbatim and AC3.2/3.3/3.4 individually. No accidental public helpers, no accidentally public state mutators outside the entry-fun set, no leaked internal-only functions. Both events `VaultCreated` and `TriggerFired` are declared `public struct ... has copy, drop, store` matching contract.md's exact field shape. The `BalanceManager` invariant (Decision Gate G-Vault: 'No `BalanceManager` is constructed or referenced anywhere in this package') is honoured — no `deepbook::balance_manager` import anywhere in `sources/`. The `swap_exact_base_for_quote_with_manager` invariant is also honoured — only the no-manager path is called. The accessor inflation issue is tracked separately (R2-003, R2-004). The entry-function-and-events surface itself is correctly minimal.
impact: None — confirms the entry-function and event surface complies with the contract verbatim.
recommendation: No action for the entry/event surface. Apply R2-003 and R2-004 fixes for the accessor surface.

title: Single-module package layout is correctly minimal; no `lib.move` indirection and no helper-module over-decomposition
description: Confirmation note: the package contains exactly one source module (`sources/tpsl_vault.move`, ~234 LOC) and one test module (`tests/tpsl_vault_tests.move`, ~489 LOC). For a 3-entry-function module with two events, three error constants, and one shared-object struct, this is the right granularity — splitting into 'types' / 'logic' / 'errors' / 'events' modules would be over-decomposition. The single-file layout matches the canonical sandbox reference `~/workspace/deepbook-sandbox/sandbox/packages/example_contract/` and Cycle 2's `slippage_swap` package (Cycle 2 R2-007 made the same observation). Section headers (`// === Error codes ===`, `// === Structs ===`, `// === Events ===`, `// === Entry functions ===`, `// === Read accessors ===`) follow the Sui convention and visually delimit the file. The module-name pair `tpsl_vault::tpsl_vault` (package::module) follows the recommended convention noted in contract.md.
impact: None — confirms package structure is appropriately minimal.
recommendation: No action. Maintain this granularity if future cycles add new functionality (e.g., a separate `tpsl_vault::events` module is unwarranted unless events grow past a 5-event surface).

title: `side: u8` is stored-and-emitted opaque metadata per Contract decision #2 — the design correctly resists assigning semantic meaning, but no in-tree comment near the field documents this
description: Per contract.md 'Contract decisions' #2, `side: u8` is stored-and-emitted opaque metadata only — `execute_trigger` does not branch on it and the Move package does not assign semantic meaning to specific `u8` values. The implementation correctly honours this: `side` is written by `create_vault` (line 86), included in `VaultCreated` (line 96), and never read again in `execute_trigger`. Correct. However, the field declaration on line 39 carries no comment explaining the opaque-metadata semantics. A future maintainer reading the source without the contract handy will see `side: u8` and may assume it has semantic meaning (e.g., 'long' vs 'short') and add validation logic (e.g., `assert!(side <= 1, EInvalidSide)`) which would silently break the keeper / UI in Cycle 3b/3c if they encode side differently. The test module pins `SIDE_LONG = 0` (line 43) but that's a test convention, not a contract-side validation. A 1-line doc-comment above the field declaration would prevent the misinterpretation.
impact: Risk that a future maintainer adds a `side` validator (e.g., `assert!(side <= 1)`) believing it's semantic, which would break the contract decision #2 invariant ('does not validate its domain'). The keeper / UI in Cycles 3b/3c are free to encode `side` however they like — adding a Move-side validator would silently constrain that.
recommendation: Add a one-line doc-comment immediately above line 39: `/// Opaque metadata; semantics defined by off-chain consumers (keeper/UI). The Move package does not validate or branch on this value (Contract decision #2).` This pins the design intent in-tree.
